status: Two rounds of independent (ChatGPT) verification of PRs #23-#25 found blocking findings before merge. All fixed on the same open PRs, with new adversarial tests. Not merged yet -- awaiting re-verification.

worker_runtime_suite.note: 44 originally -> 62 after round 1 (+18) -> 67 after round 2 (+7, minus 2 superseded end-to-end tests replaced by the round-2 pending-approval workflow tests -- net +5 over round 1's 62)

core_v2_prototypes_regression.note: unaffected by either round's fixes; unchanged from the prior 161

independent_verification_round_2_finding.finding: The round-1 approval-gates-execution fix was correct (nothing unauthorized ever executed) but incomplete: the normal WorkerClient flow had no way to represent 'legitimately waiting on approval' as anything but a hard failure -- an approval-required job reached execute(), was correctly refused because approval wasn't present yet, and poll_and_execute_once() then called submit_failure(), permanently marking a merely-pending job FAILED before a human ever had a chance to approve it.
independent_verification_round_2_finding.fix: added WorkerJobQueue.resume() alongside execute(): request_approval_if_required() parks a job (RUNNING -> WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL) without ever calling the capability's action; resume() later checks on it and, if APPROVED, delegates to execute() (never duplicated) to run it exactly once, consuming the approval into EXECUTED. A still-REQUESTED approval returns None (not an error). A DENIED/EXPIRED/CANCELLED approval ends the job safely (FAILED, not left dangling) and raises. Wired through new coordinator.request_approval()/resume_job()/deny_job() and transport.request_approval()/resume() verbs into worker_client.py's poll_and_execute_once() (now parks instead of executing/failing) and new try_resume() (checks on / executes a parked job).
tests_superseded: test_worker_client_end_to_end_refuses_unapproved_execution (asserted the now-wrong behavior -- job FAILED on an unapproved poll -- and was replaced)

test_worker_client_end_to_end_executes_once_approved (manually drove transport.execute() directly rather than the real try_resume() flow -- replaced by test_worker_client_resumes_and_executes_exactly_once_after_approval)
independent_verification_round_2_finding.bug_found_while_fixing: deny()'s and resume()'s terminal (denied/expired) paths did not release the assigned worker back to AVAILABLE, leaving it stuck BUSY indefinitely after a denial or expiry. Fixed via coordinator.deny_job() and resume_job()'s exception handling, both calling mark_available() guarded to the job's actual assigned worker only.
independent_verification_round_2_finding.explicitly_not_done: no redesign of the future network transport -- resume() inherits execute()'s exact same callable-based, in-process-only limitation, unchanged and still documented in transport.py and KARMO_WORKER_RUNTIME_NETWORK_PLAN.md

independent_verification_round_1_finding.finding: Approval gated job completion, not execution -- a worker's sandboxed handler ran unconditionally at lease time; approval state was only checked afterward at complete()
independent_verification_round_1_finding.fix: added WorkerJobQueue.execute() as the sole path to invoking a capability's action; for any authority_requirement != NONE, action() is only ever called from inside the reused ApprovalEngine.execute() (never duplicated), which validates approval state, executor identity, expiry, and an exact arguments digest, then atomically consumes the approval into EXECUTED. complete() now requires EXECUTED (was APPROVED) as defense in depth. Wired through transport.execute() into worker_client.py.
independent_verification_round_1_finding.note: the 2 end-to-end WorkerClient tests originally added alongside this fix were superseded by round 2's fix -- see independent_verification_round_2_findings_and_fixes

independent_verification_round_1_finding.finding: Timeout enforcement was a post-return elapsed-time check, not a real deadline -- a hung/CPU-bound handler was never actually interrupted
independent_verification_round_1_finding.fix: handler now runs in a forked child process under a hard deadline; on overrun the child is terminated (SIGTERM then SIGKILL) and the call fails closed
tests_added: test_scenario_14_timeout_is_a_real_kill_not_a_post_hoc_check (proves an actual kill via a marker file the handler would only write after its full sleep -- the marker never appears)
independent_verification_round_1_finding.bug_found_while_fixing: a real multiprocessing deadlock: waiting via process.join(timeout) before draining the result pipe hangs whenever a handler's result exceeds the pipe's kernel buffer (~64KB) -- the child blocks mid-write, the parent isn't reading, and every oversized-result test spuriously 'timed out'. Fixed by waiting on the connection (parent_conn.poll(timeout)) as the primary deadline gate, which starts draining as soon as data arrives.

independent_verification_round_1_finding.finding: Only stdout_summary was bounded; the structured output result and evidence_files were not
independent_verification_round_1_finding.fix: added MAX_RESULT_BYTES (64KB, refuses rather than truncates a structured dict) and MAX_EVIDENCE_FILES (20)

independent_verification_round_1_finding.finding: A worker heartbeat could set arbitrary coordinator-owned scheduling state (heartbeat(..., status=ANY_WORKERSTATUS)), letting a worker force itself AVAILABLE while actually BUSY on a live lease (or the reverse), bypassing mark_busy()/mark_available()
independent_verification_round_1_finding.fix: heartbeat() now accepts only an optional WorkerHealth (HEALTHY/DEGRADED), never a raw WorkerStatus; BUSY is untouchable by a worker's own heartbeat in either direction; DEGRADED is honored only out of non-BUSY states

defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.defect: WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL -> FAILED was not a valid transition, so a denied approval on any approval-gated job would raise an unhandled JobStateError instead of failing the job
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.found_by: exercising job_protocol.WorkerJobQueue.deny() with a synthetic approval-required capability (scenario 17's test setup)
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.fix: added JobState.FAILED to the WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL transition set, plus a new parametrized test case in job_model/tests/test_jobs.py

defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.defect: leaked the underlying job_model.JobStateError instead of wrapping it as JobProtocolError, breaking the module's own exception-boundary contract

called workers.mark_available() unconditionally; crashed with WorkerRegistryError if the worker's status wasn't exactly BUSY/DEGRADED (e.g. a job leased via WorkerJobQueue.lease() directly rather than through poll_for_job's mark_busy path) -- inconsistent with finalize_failure(), which already guarded this
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.fix: wrapped mark_available() in the same defensive try/except finalize_failure() already used

defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.defect: no module in the actual runtime path ever imported capabilities.py, so sandbox._HANDLERS would be empty (no capability could ever execute) unless something happened to import it first
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.found_by: first test run against real capability handlers (11 failures, all "no registered handler")
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.fix: worker_client.py now imports capabilities.py for its registration side effect, since it's the module that actually calls run_capability
